description: Per-namespace backup health for a tenant console. Pin $namespace per tenant when provisioning. Series: spec/05-observability.md §2; panel list: §7.

panels.title: Operator build
panels.description: This panel is the difference between an empty dashboard and a broken one. crystalbackup_build_info is a constant 1 that the operator always exports, so if THIS says No data the scrape is down and every other 'No data' below means nothing.

panels.title: Active schedules
panels.description: 1 per (schedule, origin) expected to back this namespace up. origin=cluster rows are the platform's DR schedule: visible here, but owned and edited by the platform team.

options.content:
**`origin` splits every backup panel in two.**

* `origin=namespace` — backups from *your own* `BackupSchedule`/`Backup` objects. You own them.
* `origin=cluster` — backups taken for you by the platform's `ClusterBackupSchedule` (disaster recovery). They are **read-only**: they appear in `kubectl get backups` and restore normally, but the schedule, retention and location are the platform's to change, not yours.

Freshness thresholds are the alert deadlines: amber at 24 h, red at 26 h (`CrystalbackupBackupMissed`).

panels.title: Time since last successful backup
panels.description: Per schedule, split by origin. A schedule with no series at all has never been seen by the operator — that is a missing schedule, not a healthy one.

panels.title: Backup age over time
panels.description: Sawtooth is healthy: each tooth is a successful run. A ramp that never falls is a stalled schedule.

panels.title: Backup duration — last run and p90
panels.description: Histogram buckets span 1 min to 8 h (spec §2.1), so p90 saturates at 8 h on very large first backups.

panels.title: Logical size vs bytes added (dedup)
panels.description: The gap between the two lines is what deduplication and compression saved on that run. added == logical means a full re-upload — usually a first backup or a repository reset.

panels.title: Dedup efficiency, last run
panels.description: 1 - added/logical over the last run of every schedule in this namespace.

panels.title: Data currently protected
panels.description: Logical bytes with at least one live restore point (newest recorded size per PVC).

panels.title: Bytes uploaded to the repository
panels.description: Egress estimation: deduplicated bytes actually pushed to object storage per interval.

options.content:
These panels show **your own** `BackupLocation` repository (`scope="namespace"`). The platform's shared cluster repository (`scope="cluster"`) holds the `origin=cluster` DR backups; its size, checks and prunes are platform-wide signals and are deliberately not exposed here. If you have no `BackupLocation` of your own, this whole row is legitimately empty — the *Backup freshness* row above is the one that must not be.

The first line answers *what is in the repository, and is my view of it current*; the second, *when was it last verified and maintained*.

panels.title: Repository size
panels.description: Physical size in object storage, post-dedup and post-compression — the objects the bucket bills you for. There is deliberately no second 'stored bytes' figure beside it: one measurement, one name (spec §2.11).

panels.title: Snapshots in repository
panels.description: What restic actually holds. Compare with *Backups projected* to its right.

panels.title: Backups projected
panels.description: What `kubectl get backups` lists for this repository. Read it against *Snapshots in repository*: the two count different things — snapshots are per volume, a projected Backup groups a whole run — so they are not meant to be equal. What matters is that this one MOVES when the other does. Frozen while snapshots climb means discovery has stopped projecting, and your list of restore points is stale.

panels.title: Discovery health
panels.description: Discovery is the projection from the repository into the `Backup` objects you can see. The check and prune panels below say whether your repository is INTACT; this one says whether what you are LOOKING AT still matches it. Failing means your restore-point list is silently stale — short of what exists, or naming snapshots that no longer do.

panels.title: Last check result
panels.description: Absent until the first restic check has actually run — absence is 'not measured yet', not 0 (spec §2.4).

panels.title: Since last prune
panels.description: Absent by design on Immutable locations, which never prune (ADR 0005).

panels.title: Since last discovery scan
panels.description: A scan that stopped running is the other way the projection goes stale, alongside one that runs and fails.

panels.title: Stale locks
panels.description: Locks older than restic's 30-minute threshold. Normally reaped back to 0; a persistent non-zero blocks maintenance.

panels.title: Repository size over time
panels.description: Physical bytes under your repository prefix. A step up after each backup, a step down after a prune.

panels.title: Restores currently in a failed state
panels.description: Restore objects sitting in Failed or PartiallyFailed right now — still describable with kubectl.

panels.title: Restores completed, by mode
panels.description: mode is Recreate or Overwrite. The mode label lives on the duration histogram and the failure counter only — the last-success and last-bytes gauges above carry origin, not mode (spec §2.3).

panels.title: Restore failures by mode
panels.description: AwaitingConfirmation is not counted here — it is the system asking a question, not a failure (R23).

panels.title: Backups currently in a failed state
panels.description: Failed Backup objects that still EXIST in the namespace — the wreckage you can `kubectl describe` right now. Metric cardinality is bounded per (schedule, origin), so this cannot name individual Backup objects; use `kubectl get backups -n $namespace` for that.

panels.title: Backups that reached a failed phase
panels.description: Counter of transitions into Failed/PartiallyFailed — this is what the BackupFailed alert reads.

panels.title: Backup outcomes over the selected range
panels.description: result is completed | partiallyfailed | failed.

panels.title: Mover job retries
panels.description: Mover pod retries consumed against the Job backoffLimit for this namespace. Sustained retries usually mean a storage class that stalls or a volume too big for the window.
